sentences.text: This ancient fish possessed heavily armored heads and front bodies, while its tails remained unarmored and covered in scales.
It was among the first species recognized as distinct, with fossils common in the Old Red Sandstone formation studied since the early 19th century.
The creature remained an unsolved puzzle due to its extreme divergence from modern fish until Charles Darwin proposed evolutionary theories.
The genus was described by Bleeker in 1859.
The type species of the genus is Pterichthyodes milleri.
Fossils of this animal have been found in Scotland.
Fossils suggest Pterichthyodes was a bottom-dweller that crawled on lake beds using its pectoral appendages.
It is theorized that Pterichthyodes used its appendages to bury itself in the sediment.
Pterichthyodes likely fed by browsing shallow lake beds for decaying detritus.
The animal may have fed by moving through shallow lake beds searching for decaying detritus.
Pterichthyodes belongs to the family Asterolepididae.
The genus is classified within the order Antiarchi.
As placoderms, these creatures were among the earliest vertebrates to possess jaws, but they had grinding plates instead of teeth.
The name Pterichthyodes refers to the genus's unique wing-like appendages.
Pterichthyodes is easily distinguished from other placoderms by its strange wing-shaped appendages.
Pterichthyodes lived during the Devonian period.
The animal lived from the Eifelian to the Givetian stages, between 393.47 and 382.31 million years ago.
